mainTopic: Whether loaves and wafers of a מנחת מאפה may be mixed, the end of פרק כל המנחות, and the opening משנה on reaping the עומר on שבת.
overview: The amud begins at the end of a ברייתא about the מנחת מאפה, which can be made as loaves (חלות) or wafers (רקיקין). רבי שמעון says the פסוק writes קרבן only once, so loaves and wafers are one offering and may even be mixed half and half. רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה learns from the repeated word וכל that they are two separate types and may not be mixed. The גמרא then shows how רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון each explain the double בשמן in the פסוק. It also explains how רבי יוסי differs from his father: for the son, a mixed offering is not valid even after the fact. Then פרק כל המנחות ends, and a new פרק opens with a משנה about how much barley was reaped for the עומר on שבת and on a weekday. רבא explains that רבי ישמעאל uses less barley on שבת so there is less total work. רבה compares this to a ruling about skinning the פסח on שבת. The גמרא starts to reject that comparison, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The word 'offering' appears only once
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון points out that the פסוק says קרבן only one time, and both חלות and רקיקין are listed under it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does the verse say 'offering' twice, once for loaves and once for wafers? No. It says 'offering' only once, and under that one word it lists both loaves and wafers.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון finishes his proof from the wording of the פסוק. Because קרבן is written only once, loaves and wafers are two forms of the same offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תורה had written קרבן separately for loaves and for wafers, they would be two separate offerings. Since the תורה wrote קרבן only once and listed both forms under it, they belong to one single מנחה. This sets up his practical ruling in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering. Here, the key word in the פסוק that shows how many offerings there are.
Thick loaves, one form of the oven-baked מנחה.
Thin wafers, the other form of the oven-baked מנחה.
But isn't it so that... (introduces an obvious counter-fact).

steps.confusionAlert: The question 'is קרבן said twice?' is not a real question. It is רבי שמעון's way of making his point: obviously it is said only once.

phrases.english: And is 'offering,' 'offering' stated two times?

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲלֹא לֹא נֶאֱמַר אֶלָּא קׇרְבָּן אֶחָד,
phrases.english: But isn't 'offering' stated only one time,
and both loaves and wafers are stated with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי שמעון's argument from the part of the ברייתא that comes just before this section.
steps.raayaObject: That חלות and רקיקין are one single offering.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The single word קרבן in ויקרא 2:4, which covers both loaves and wafers.

steps.title: Loaves, wafers, or half and half are all acceptable
steps.stepSummary: Since it is one offering, רבי שמעון rules that a person may bring all loaves, all wafers, or half of each. A handful taken from only one kind still counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: So from now on: if he wants to bring loaves, he may. If he wants wafers, he may. Half loaves and half wafers, he may. He mixes them together and takes a handful from both. And if he took a handful and it came up from only one kind, it counts for both, and he has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון draws the practical result of his proof. Because loaves and wafers are one offering, they can be combined in any way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מעתה tells us this rule follows directly from step 1. Since both forms make up one מנחה, the קמיצה (taking the handful) can come from either kind and still cover the whole offering. You don't need some of each in the handful.

keyTerms.meaning: From now / therefore. Draws a result from what was just proven.
Half.
He mixes them together.
Takes a קמיצה, the handful removed from a מנחה to be burned on the מזבח.
He has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון, a מנחת מאפה is one offering. So a person may mix loaves and wafers, and a handful from either kind counts for the whole offering.

phrases.english: From now: if he wants to bring loaves, he brings them;
wafers, he brings them;
half loaves and half wafers, he brings them;
and he mixes them and takes a handful from both of them;
and if he took a handful and there came up in his hand
only one kind for both of them, he has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical ruling from the proof in step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Loaves and wafers may be brought separately or combined, and a קמיצה from one kind counts for both.

steps.title: רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה asks for the source against mixing
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה takes the opposite view and asks where we learn that a person may not bring half loaves and half wafers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה says: From where do we know that one who says 'I take upon myself a baked מנחה' may not bring half loaves and half wafers?
steps.whatsHappening: A new תנא gives the opposing view. He asks for the source, and the גמרא is setting up his answer from the פסוק in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון allowed half and half. רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה assumes it is forbidden and asks only where the source is. So the argument now turns to which פסוק decides the question.

keyTerms.meaning: From where (do we learn this)? Asks for a source.
'It is upon me.' The words used to take on a נדר to bring an offering.
The oven-baked meal offering.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Yehuda says:
From where do we know, regarding one who says 'It is upon me to bring a baked meal offering,'

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יָבִיא מֶחֱצָה חַלּוֹת וּמֶחֱצָה רְקִיקִין?
phrases.english: that he may not bring half loaves and half wafers?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: מִנַּיִן לְאוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי שמעון's ruling in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that forbids bringing a מנחת מאפה as half loaves and half wafers.

steps.title: The verses about 'and every' meal offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה quotes ויקרא 7:9–10, which use the word וכל for several kinds of מנחות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And every meal offering that is baked in the oven, and every one made in the deep pan and on the flat pan, shall belong to the כהן who offers it. And every meal offering mixed with oil, or dry, shall belong to all the sons of Aharon.'
steps.whatsHappening: He gives his source: two פסוקים that keep using the word וכל ('and every'). In the next step he explains how they prove his point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key is the word וכל, which shows up in both פסוקים. The oven-baked מנחה is in the first פסוק, the 'upper' one. The second, 'lower' פסוק has וכל for 'mixed with oil' and 'dry'. This prepares a comparison between the two.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches. Introduces the source.
'And every.' The repeated word the proof is built on.
Deep pan.
Flat pan / griddle.
Dry, meaning without oil.

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְכׇל מִנְחָה אֲשֶׁר תֵּאָפֶה בַּתַּנּוּר״,
phrases.english: The verse states: 'And every meal offering that is baked in the oven,'
'and every one made in the deep pan and on the flat pan'
'shall belong to the priest who offers it,'
'and every meal offering mixed with oil, or dry,'
'shall belong to all the sons of Aharon.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְכׇל מִנְחָה אֲשֶׁר תֵּאָפֶה בַּתַּנּוּר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3 by bringing the פסוקים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is ויקרא 7:9–10, with its repeated word וכל.

steps.title: Just as below, so above: two separate types
steps.stepSummary: He compares the two uses of וכל. In the lower פסוק it covers two different kinds, so in the upper פסוק loaves and wafers are also two different kinds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as 'and every' stated below refers to two separate types, so too 'and every' stated above refers to two separate types.
steps.whatsHappening: He finishes his proof by comparing the two פסוקים. Loaves and wafers are two separate types, so they cannot be mixed in one offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ויקרא 7:10, 'mixed with oil' and 'dry' are clearly two different מנחות. Because the same word וכל appears in 7:9, he reads the two forms of the oven-baked מנחה the same way, as two distinct types. That directly opposes רבי שמעון's 'one offering' reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as... so too... The form of a comparison between two cases.
Below / above. The later פסוק and the earlier פסוק.
Two separate, distinct types.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון holds that loaves and wafers are one offering, so mixing is allowed. רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה holds they are two separate types, learned from וכל, so mixing is not allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: The argument decides whether a person who vowed a מנחת מאפה must choose either all loaves or all wafers.

phrases.english: Just as the 'and every' stated below
phrases.notes: 'Below' is ויקרא 7:10, where 'mixed with oil' and 'dry' are two different kinds of מנחה.

phrases.english: refers to two separate types,
so too the 'and every' stated above
refers to two separate types.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוקים quoted in step 4 prove the ruling asked about in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That loaves and wafers of a מנחת מאפה are two separate types and cannot be mixed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Comparing the word וכל in ויקרא 7:9 with the same word in ויקרא 7:10.

steps.title: How does רבי יהודה deal with רבי שמעון's proof?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה: רבי שמעון's proof from the single word קרבן seems strong, so how does רבי יהודה answer it?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה? Isn't רבי שמעון making a good point?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבי יהודה, who holds that חלות and רקיקין are two separate kinds. It asks how he can disagree when רבי שמעון's proof sounds so good. This sets up the next step, where רבי יהודה answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון proved from the single word קרבן that loaves and wafers are one offering (Step 1). רבי יהודה holds they are two kinds, so he must have some way to answer that proof. The גמרא is pushing him to explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: He is saying it well; he makes a good point

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: He means: how does רבי יהודה, who says loaves and wafers are two kinds, answer this?

phrases.english: isn't Rabbi Shimon saying it well?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, שַׁפִּיר קָאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי שמעון's proof from Step 1 and challenges the opposing view to answer it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's view that חלות and רקיקין are two separate kinds
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says קרבן only once over both kinds, which suggests they form one offering.

steps.title: Double בשמן counts like a double קרבן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה answers that the פסוק says בשמן twice, once for the loaves and once for the wafers. That is like saying קרבן twice, so they are two offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: He could tell you: since it says 'with oil' and again 'with oil,' it is as if it said 'offering' and again 'offering.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה answers the challenge. Each kind gets its own mention of בשמן, so the פסוק treats them as two separate offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה agrees that קרבן is written only once. But the separate בשמן for each kind splits them apart just as two separate words קרבן would. So for him the single קרבן does not prove they are one offering.

keyTerms.meaning: With oil; written once for the loaves and once for the wafers
It is as if it were written...; treated like

phrases.english: He could say to you:
since it is written 'with oil' and 'with oil,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:4: loaves 'mixed with oil' and wafers 'spread with oil.'

phrases.english: it is as though it is written 'offering' and 'offering.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 6 on behalf of רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counter-reading of the פסוק: a different repeated word does the job of a repeated קרבן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The single word קרבן shows that loaves and wafers are one offering.
steps.terutzMaskana: The double בשמן makes them two offerings, as if קרבן were written twice.

steps.title: What does רבי שמעון do with the double בשמן?
steps.stepSummary: Now the גמרא turns to רבי שמעון: if בשמן is written twice, what does he learn from it?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the other side the same kind of question. רבי שמעון must explain the double בשמן if it does not split the kinds into two offerings. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה used the double בשמן to show two separate offerings. רבי שמעון holds it is one offering, so he must explain why the פסוק repeats the word.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon?
phrases.notes: He means: what does רבי שמעון do with the double 'with oil' that רבי יהודה just used?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רבי יהודה's source from Step 7 back against רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's view that loaves and wafers are one offering
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק repeats בשמן, which seems to separate the kinds. רבי שמעון needs another purpose for that repetition.

steps.title: Double בשמן teaches that one kind alone is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says the double בשמן teaches that loaves alone or wafers alone are allowed. Without it, we would have thought you must bring exactly half of each.
steps.simpleTranslation: If 'with oil' were not written twice, I would have said you must bring exactly half loaves and half wafers, and that loaves alone or wafers alone are not allowed. So the פסוק teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives the double בשמן its own job. It shows that each kind may also be brought alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since קרבן is written once over both kinds, one might have thought the offering needs both kinds together, half and half. The separate בשמן for each kind shows that each one can also stand alone. So רבי שמעון reaches his full rule from Step 2: all loaves, all wafers, or half of each.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have said; the mistaken first thought
Specifically; only this way
By themselves; alone
It teaches us (that the first thought is wrong)

steps.confusionAlert: Here רבי שמעון does NOT use the double בשמן to separate the two kinds the way רבי יהודה does. He uses it to show that one kind alone is also fine. The 'half and half only' idea was just the mistaken first thought (הוה אמינא), not his ruling.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: the double בשמן makes loaves and wafers two offerings. רבי שמעון: it is one offering, and the double בשמן shows you may bring one kind alone.

phrases.english: If it were not written 'with oil' and 'with oil,'
I would have said that only
half loaves and half wafers are allowed,
but loaves by themselves
or wafers by themselves, I would say not,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 8 by giving the double בשמן a different purpose.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the extra word a different teaching (הוה אמינא / קא משמע לן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the double בשמן, one would think the offering must be exactly half loaves and half wafers.
steps.terutzMaskana: The double בשמן teaches that loaves alone or wafers alone are also valid.

steps.title: Isn't רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה the same as his father?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה is quoted separately if he seems to say the same thing as his father, רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה's view the same as his father's?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that father and son both say loaves and wafers are two kinds. It asks what the son adds. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both רבי יהודה and his son רבי יוסי (Steps 3-5) treat חלות and רקיקין as separate kinds. If their views are the same, there is no need to quote both. So there must be some real difference.

keyTerms.meaning: That is the same as

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הַיְינוּ אֲבוּהּ?
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda is the same as his father?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הַיְינוּ אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the רבי יהודה / רבי שמעון discussion to compare רבי יהודה with his son.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical difference there is between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה

steps.title: They differ when someone already mixed them
steps.stepSummary: The difference is a case where someone already brought half loaves and half wafers. For רבי יהודה the offering is still valid after the fact. For his son it is not valid even then.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them in a case where he already did it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that father and son really do differ. The difference is a case where someone already mixed the two kinds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that you should not mix loaves and wafers to begin with. רבי יהודה holds that if someone already did, the offering is valid (בדיעבד). רבי יוסי holds that a mixed offering is not valid even after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
Where he already did it; after the fact
After the fact, once it was already done

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: mixing is wrong at first, but valid if already done. רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה: mixing is not valid even after the fact.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them where he already did it.
phrases.notes: He means someone already brought half loaves and half wafers. רבי יהודה says it is valid; his son says it is not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10 by naming the practical difference.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They differ in a case where someone already mixed the two kinds: valid for רבי יהודה, not valid for רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק כל המנחות
steps.stepSummary: The פרק כל המנחות ends with the traditional closing line.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק כל המנחות.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing line of the chapter. It marks the end of פרק כל המנחות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הדרן עלך is the standard line said at the end of each פרק. It shows love for the chapter and a hope to come back and learn it again.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you; the closing line said at the end of a chapter

phrases.english: We will return to you, Kol HaMenachot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final discussion.

steps.title: Opening משנה: three or five סאין of barley for the עומר
steps.stepSummary: The new פרק opens with a מחלוקת. רבי ישמעאל says the עומר comes from three סאין of barley on שבת and five on a weekday. The חכמים say it is always three.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי ישמעאל says: the עומר would come from three סאין on שבת and from five on a weekday. The חכמים say: on שבת and on a weekday alike, it would come from three.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins with a משנה about how much barley was reaped to make the עומר offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל makes the amount depend on the day: less barley on שבת, more on a weekday. The חכמים say the day makes no difference and the amount is always three סאין. The משנה doesn't explain either side; the גמרא will look into that.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley offering brought on the second day of פסח
A measure of volume (plural: סאין)
A regular weekday, as opposed to שבת
The משנה being studied

phrases.english: Mishnah:
Rabbi Yishmael says:

phrases.aramaic: עוֹמֶר הָיָה בָּא בַּשַּׁבָּת מִשָּׁלֹשׁ סְאִין,
phrases.english: The omer would come on Shabbat from three se'ah,
and on a weekday from five.
And the Sages say:
Both on Shabbat and on a weekday,
it would come from three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק right after the הדרן closing the previous one in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ישמעאל: three סאין on שבת, five on a weekday. חכמים: three on both.

steps.title: משנה continues: how many people reap the עומר
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים says that on שבת the barley was reaped by one person with one sickle and one basket, and on a weekday by three people with three sickles and three baskets. The חכמים say it is always three.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים says: on שבת it was reaped by one person, with one sickle and one basket. On a weekday it was reaped by three people, with three baskets and three sickles. The חכמים say: on שבת and on a weekday alike, by three people, with three baskets and three sickles.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a second מחלוקת, this time about how the reaping was done rather than how much barley was used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא, like רבי ישמעאל, does less on שבת and more on a weekday. The חכמים again say the day changes nothing. The two halves of the משנה follow the same pattern.

keyTerms.meaning: The deputy of the כהן גדול
Was reaped (cut down)
A sickle, a curved blade for cutting grain
A basket

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina, the deputy of the Kohanim, says:
On Shabbat it was reaped by one person,
and with one sickle, and with one basket,
and on a weekday, by three people,
with three baskets and three sickles.
And the Sages say:
Both on Shabbat and on a weekday, by three people,
with three baskets and with three sickles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, parallel מחלוקת to the משנה, about how the reaping is done.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנינא: on שבת, one reaper, one sickle, one basket; on a weekday, three of each. חכמים: three of each on both.

steps.title: The גמרא grants that the view of the חכמים makes sense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the חכמים are easy to understand. They hold that a choice עשרון of flour comes from three סאין, so there is no reason for שבת to be different from a weekday.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The view of the חכמים makes sense. They hold that a choice עשרון comes from three סאין, and there is no difference between a weekday and שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by agreeing that the חכמים' view is clear. This sets up the next move, which is a question on רבי ישמעאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עומר needs an עשרון of high-quality flour, and the חכמים hold that three סאין of barley are enough to produce it. Since the requirement is the same every day, the amount is the same every day. The word בשלמא signals that a contrast is coming: the other opinion is harder to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense for... (sets up a coming question on the other side)
A choice, top-quality tenth of an איפה of flour
There is no difference
The discussion of the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is finished with the חכמים here and moving to a new topic. בשלמא is only the first half of a single question. It grants one side so it can push hard on the other side in the next step.

phrases.english: Gemara:
It makes sense for the Rabbis, since they hold:
a choice tenth comes from three se'ah,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets, 'from three,' is the corrected wording. The meaning is the same.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא שְׁנָא בְּחוֹל וְלָא שְׁנָא בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: and there is no difference between a weekday and Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא starts analyzing the first מחלוקת of the משנה, beginning with the easier opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים hold that a choice עשרון comes from three סאין regardless of the day.

steps.title: Challenge: why does רבי ישמעאל split between שבת and weekday?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי ישמעאל. If a choice עשרון needs five סאין, it should need five on שבת too. If three are enough, three should be enough on a weekday too.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי ישמעאל, what does he hold? If he holds a choice עשרון comes only from five, then five should be needed even on שבת! If it can come from three, then three should be enough even on a weekday!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי ישמעאל with a two-sided question. Either way, his distinction between שבת and a weekday seems to make no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether five or three סאין are needed should not depend on the day, since the flour must meet the same standard every time. If five are needed, three on שבת would not be enough. If three are enough, why bother with five on a weekday?

keyTerms.meaning: What does he hold? What is his reasoning?
If this... and if that... (a two-sided challenge)
Even... as well

phrases.english: But Rabbi Yishmael, what does he hold?
If he holds that a choice tenth
comes only from five se'ah,
then even on Shabbat too it should be five!
And if it can come from three,
then even on a weekday too three should be enough!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the בשלמא setup of step 15 by turning to the harder opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's split between three סאין on שבת and five on a weekday.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The amount needed for a choice עשרון is a fixed fact. So either five are always needed or three are always enough, and the day should not matter.

steps.title: רבא explains why רבי ישמעאל treats שבת differently
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that a choice עשרון can come from five סאין with little effort, or from three סאין with extra sifting. On a weekday we use five because that is nicer. On שבת we use three, because it is better to do more of one job (sifting) than to multiply many jobs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רבי ישמעאל holds that a choice עשרון comes from five סאין without much effort, and from three סאין with effort. On a weekday we bring it from five, because that way is nicer. On שבת it is better to do a lot of one job, sifting, than to do a lot of many jobs.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge from the last step by showing that both three and five סאין really can give a choice עשרון. The difference is only how much work it takes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed there is only one right amount of barley. רבא says both amounts work. Five סאין needs little sifting, while three סאין needs a lot of extra sifting. On שבת, reaping more barley would mean more reaping, threshing and grinding, so it is better to take less barley and just sift it more.

keyTerms.meaning: Extra effort or bother
Nicer, of better quality
It is better
Sifting flour through a sieve

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying three סאין gives worse flour. Both amounts give the same choice עשרון. Three סאין just needs more sifting to get there.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer sets up the idea that on שבת we try to keep the total amount of work small. רבה builds on that idea in the next step.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Rabbi Yishmael holds:
a choice tenth, without extra effort,
comes from five se'a;
with effort, it comes from three.
On a weekday we bring it from five,
because that way the thing is nicer.
On Shabbat, it is better that he do more
of one labor, the sifting,
and not do more of many labors.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 16 against רבי ישמעאל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both amounts are valid; the difference is how much effort each one takes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A choice עשרון needs one fixed amount of barley, so שבת and weekdays should match
steps.terutzMaskana: Five סאין without effort, or three סאין with extra sifting. On שבת we choose the way with fewer kinds of labor.

steps.title: רבה links רבי ישמעאל to the ruling on skinning the פסח on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבה says that רבי ישמעאל and רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה hold the same idea. He brings a ברייתא: when the fourteenth of ניסן falls on שבת, the second רבי ישמעאל rules that the פסח is skinned only down to the breast. The חכמים say it must be skinned completely.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: רבי ישמעאל and רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה said the same thing. A ברייתא teaches: when the fourteenth of ניסן falls on שבת, he skins the פסח down to the breast. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. The חכמים say: he must skin all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה opens a new point. He compares רבי ישמעאל's view on the עומר to a ruling by a different sage with the same name, about the פסח on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two different sages here who are both named רבי ישמעאל. The ברייתא shows that רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה allows only partial skinning on שבת, while the חכמים require full skinning. רבה is claiming that both sages named רבי ישמעאל share one approach. The next step explains what that approach is.

keyTerms.meaning: The same thing, one shared idea
The fourteenth of ניסן, the day the קרבן פסח is brought
Skins, removes the hide of an animal
The breast of the animal

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two names. 'רבי ישמעאל' of the עומר and 'רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה' are two different sages.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Yishmael

phrases.aramaic: בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה
phrases.english: son of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka
said the same thing, as it is taught:
When the fourteenth of Nisan falls on Shabbat,
one skins the Pesaḥ offering down to the breast,
these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael

phrases.aramaic: בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה.
phrases.english: son of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka.
And the Rabbis say:
until he skins all of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אָמְרוּ דָּבָר אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבא's explanation by connecting רבי ישמעאל's view to a parallel ruling about the פסח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both sages named רבי ישמעאל share one approach. The second one rules that on שבת the פסח is skinned only down to the breast.

steps.title: The shared principle: we do not add work on שבת when it is not needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רבה's comparison. רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה holds that whenever we can manage without extra work on שבת, we do not do the extra work. The same reason explains the עומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה say there that wherever it is possible, we do not put in extra effort? Here too, since it is possible, we do not put in extra effort.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out why רבה said the two sages hold the same thing. Both avoid extra work on שבת whenever the job can be done without it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסח case, skinning down to the breast is enough to take out the parts for the מזבח, so the rest of the skinning is not done on שבת. In the עומר case, three סאין are enough, so reaping five is not done on שבת. One rule covers both cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Wherever it is possible to manage without it
We do not put in extra effort
There, meaning the other case (here, the פסח)
Here too, meaning the current case (here, the עומר)

steps.whyThisMatters: This states the shared principle clearly, so the next step can test whether the two cases are really alike.

phrases.english: Didn't Rabbi Yishmael

phrases.aramaic: בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה הָתָם,
phrases.english: son of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka say there,
that wherever it is possible,
we do not put in extra effort?
Here too, since it is possible,
we do not put in extra effort.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי לָא אָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבה's comparison in step 18.
steps.raayaObject: That both sages named רבי ישמעאל hold the same principle
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling of רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה about skinning the פסח only down to the breast on שבת

steps.title: Maybe the פסח case is different because of disgrace to holy things
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רבה's comparison. Perhaps רבי ישמעאל limits work only in the עומר case, where nothing holy is disgraced. In the פסח case, leaving the animal half-skinned would be a disgrace to holy things. The sentence continues on the next daf.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do you know this? Perhaps רבי ישמעאל only said his ruling here, where there is no disgrace to holy things. But there, where there is a disgrace to holy things...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to reject רבה's comparison by pointing to a difference between the two cases. The argument is not finished yet and continues on the next daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the עומר, taking only three סאין does no harm to anything holy. With the פסח, leaving a holy animal half-skinned is disrespectful to it. So the רבי ישמעאל of the עומר might agree with the חכמים that the פסח should be skinned completely. If so, the two sages do not really share one view.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know this?
Perhaps, maybe
He only said his ruling in this case and no further
Disgrace or disrespect to holy offerings

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'רבי ישמעאל' with no other name means the sage of the עומר. 'Here' is the עומר case and 'there' is the פסח case.

phrases.english: From where do you know this?
Perhaps he only said it
Rabbi Yishmael, here,
where there is no disgrace to holy things,
but there, where there is disgrace to holy things,

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי? דִּלְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל הָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back against the comparison made in steps 18 and 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the two sages named רבי ישמעאל must hold the same view
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסח case involves disgrace to holy things, which the עומר case does not, so one sage's ruling cannot prove the other's view
